head: ChatGPT shopping answers can point to fake online stores, study says
dek: About 9% of 6,795 shopping answers from ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity named fake, suspicious or dead shopping sites, a study by US brand-protection firm Podqi found. Perplexity did so in 15% of its answers, ChatGPT in 8% and Gemini in 4%.
details: The researchers checked 4,437 web addresses that came up in the answers and flagged 718 as risky: 351 fraudulent and 367 no longer working. Fake stores, counterfeit sellers and sites pretending to be well-known brands counted as fraudulent. In answers that named a risky site, the chatbot recommended it 57% of the time and warned against it 9% of the time. Questions about shipping abroad or a store for one country gave the most risky results, 16%. OpenAI said it is working on stronger safeguards; Google said Gemini can be wrong and shows source links so people can check.
where: ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity; study reported on 14 November
means: If you ask a chatbot where to buy something for the holidays, a shop it names may not be real, even when the link looks right.
todo: Open the sources under the chatbot's answer and check the full web address before you pay. Be most careful with country-specific or overseas stores of a big brand, which came up most in the study.
thumb_words: CHATBOTS CAN SEND YOU TO FAKE SHOPS
